scores.arm: A geoset_fov_ft (global FOV rectangle crop: memory mask AND tokens outside R dropped, p=0.5)
scores.note: About 150 lines across augment.py, wrapper drop field, train hook and arms/preset/TAG append. The decode path is untouched and the Z4 Fencing --xcl out byte check covers the adopted path. Training is about 3.0-3.2 h. scores.arm: B geoset_cut_ft (FOV crop or interior HOLE, 1/2 each at p=0.5)

scores.note: Already decoded and scored (geoset_pred_ft_rep_x_e11, J&F 0.9148). It is only re-scored in the chain, at zero GPU cost.

It also needs a CLI _raw aux folder in run_all, check_preflight and leak guard for both checkpoints, and a stage1_supply record/MANIFEST that today carries a single arm and ckpt_sha256. restore_init after DEC arms is already tested (test_e9_decoder.py:168), but the registered Z3 checks only Fencing, so 'base after the previous scene's ext decode' is never byte-checked. scores.note: Needs both the token-drop infrastructure (as M) and the compose infrastructure, so realistically about 2 days of implementation. scores.note: Needs the losses weight= path, an in-loop Pi3 reprojection in data.load_sample (+35 ms per step, +4.5 %), and the compose infrastructure. The design-minimal loss-mass measurement already puts 76 % (in-sample) and 95 % (held-out) of the focal mass in the invisible region, and lambda=2 only moves that to about 0.88, so a null is expected. The registered tie order (N0 > M_c > W_c) makes it practically unadoptable over N0. The change is training-only; decode is untouched.

refuted_claims: Design 2 M_c cost: 'training about 2.85 h, no extra compute; the per-object mask is already paid in today's gated steps'. The geoset_pred_ft logs (5 folds) show 2-view steps with a per-object gate mask average 1.03 s against 0.79 s ungated. Only 34.8 % of steps carry that mask today, so p=0.5 dropout adds it on about 1/3 more steps, giving about +5-8 % (about 3.0-3.1 h). That matches E9's trained arms at 2.98-3.05 h.

Design 1 cost basis: the mask is 'already materialised on the ~20 % conf-gated steps today'. The 0.18-0.22 figure is gated_frac, the per-object fraction. The per-step share with a materialised [B,1,Lq,SumL] mask is 34.8 % (4,679 of 13,464 steps). Design 1's overall estimate (+8 % for M, +15 % for M+) still holds.

Train-pipeline analyst: 'tests_torch/test_train_smoke.py:168-223 already tests this kind of [rng-stream byte] identity'. Those lines are the set2 smoke test, the all-gated test and the no-grad-into-prediction test. The only stream-identity test is the host-side tests/test_geomem_data.py:117 (memory_rng leaves the main stream alone). No test asserts that loss columns reproduce across runs, so design 0's 'pre/post 20-step loss/n_mem/gated_frac columns identical' check assumes bit-deterministic bf16 training, which nothing has established.

Design 2: 'vis is already computed per target camera for the reproj gate, so the rule costs ~0 beyond the second decode'. run.reproj_overlap computes valid internally but returns only (overlap, n_valid). vis must be recomputed (project_reference_masks, about 35 ms per camera), or reproj_overlap's return signature changed. The latter touches the adopted decode function and needs a byte check.

Design 2: N0 is 'measured at design time' at +0.0011 [+0.0005, +0.0018]. The measurement used a different rule from the registered one. null_compose.py builds U only from the scored objects of each camera, which leaves out 13 C0 masks in 10 of 34 cameras; the registered U is all C0 masks, hallucinations included. It also used the non-xcl geoset_dec_ft_rep_e9 folder, while the registered N0 uses an xcl decode. And the null was chosen after measuring three nulls on the same 664 pairs.

Design 0 spec: 'MemorySet.subset(): slice drop[:, i] like conf'. drop is [B, 5184], so selecting objects means drop[i]. Harmless in practice, because the chunked subset path runs only at decode, where drop is None.
blocking_issues: Design 2 as registered does not fit a one-day implementation plus a chain of 10 h or less. Training M_c and W_c takes about 6.1-6.4 h. Three composed decodes (base + ext each, about 16 min) add about 0.8 h. N0 passes G1 almost certainly, so its stage-2 sweep (about 1.9 h with the doubled in-process stage 1) is effectively guaranteed. Add M_c's sweep and the chain is about 10.8 h; with all three, about 12.7 h. The compose path also needs decode_scene/Stage1.run support for two checkpoints, a CLI _raw aux folder in run_all, check_preflight and leak guard for both checkpoints, a two-checkpoint stage1_supply record/MANIFEST, and tests. That is more than a day.

Design 2's two-model in-process path: the registered Z3 byte check uses Fencing only, so it never exercises 'base geoset_pred_ft decode after the previous scene's ext (DEC-arm) decode in the same process'. That ordering is what the CLI run_all and the 17-scene stage-2 sweep do. A cross-order check on two or more scenes is required, plus two-checkpoint provenance, before any composed preset reaches STAGE1=<tag>.

Design 0's rng spec is self-contradictory. code_changes calls sample_cut(aug_rng(a.seed, step)) and labels it 'the second draw from the same generator', but that re-creates the generator. Implemented literally, the coin u<0.5 becomes sample_cut's first draw: arm B's mode draw is then always 'fov' (B silently equals A), and A's first side draw is biased. This must be fixed, with a host histogram test of mode and side, before any training.
verdicts.recommendation:
From the engineering side, register design 1's arm set {C0, M (p=0.5), M+ (p=1.0)} as S1-E12.

Why it fits:
- It touches one shared inference symbol: MemoryView.drop, read only by MemorySet.gate_mask (stage1/geomem/wrapper.py:81-94). With drop=None the adopted path stays byte-identical by construction; the decode path (methods/geomem/run.py) is unchanged.
- Stage1 PRESETS (stage1/methods/geomem/stage1.py) and SCSam3/stage1_supply.py TAGS are append-only, so in-process parity needs no new code path.
- M+ costs no extra code and gives dose-response.
- About 120 lines plus tests is realistic for one day.
- Chain timing, from the E9/E11 logs: the stage-1 half is about 6.9 h (train M about 3.05 h, M+ about 3.3 h, two 8-min decodes, eval/seedfail/visibility about 0.3 h). One passing arm adds a 1 h 42 min sweep, about 8.6 h in total. If both pass (P about 0.1-0.15) it is about 10.3 h, so run the second sweep separately.

Fixes before registering:
1. Replace design 1's test (d) and design 0's 'pre/post loss columns identical' check. Nothing establishes that bf16 training is bit-deterministic, and log.csv records neither object subsets nor coins. Use:
   - a host test that cut_rng [seed, step, 1] leaves memory_rng and the shared rng untouched (the tests/test_geomem_data.py:117 pattern);
   - per-step logged cut, n_cut, cut_frac and the drawn object ids;
   - an in-process forward-identity test with drop=None on the Blocks _pred_batch;
   - a gate_mask test with -inf exactly on the dropped feature columns and never on pointer columns.
2. Keep Z4 as an actual run: Fencing --arm geoset_pred_ft --gate reproj --xcl out against geoset_pred_ft_rep_x_e11 (final, r1, round1_conf, xcl_conf). MVSeed/inproc_check.py only compares existing _ip folders and does not run the modified code.
3. Abort guards: any fold wall above 1.15 x the adopted fold (about 2,560 s), trainable_params other than 5,922,321, or decode not 17/17.
4. Expect a modest effect. Raw trained arms have P(G1) about 0.3 against a retrain-noise half-width of about 0.0025. Report the visibility-recall and FP-split diagnostics (move train_vis.py to MVSeed/refloss/e12) as mechanism evidence, not as gates.

What to drop or defer:
- Drop design 0 arm B (hole spill, and the rng spec bug that can silently turn it into A).
- Drop design 2 arm W_c (the loss-mass measurement already closes it).
- Design 0 arm A is a reasonable alternative to M+ (a global rectangle more faithful to a narrower FOV), but it needs the extra mask-crop path and fixes to its rng and subset spec slips.
- Keep design 2's composition shell (N0, M_c) out of this chain. It is an untrained two-checkpoint ensemble, and its +0.0011 was measured post hoc on a neighbouring rule. Adopting it would add a permanent second-model path to the in-process pipeline. If the user wants it, register it as its own decode-only experiment (about 16 min decode plus one sweep). Do that only after implementing compose with a two-scene cross-order byte check, two-checkpoint preflight and provenance, and U taken from all C0 masks.

scores.arm: A geoset_fov_ft (rectangle FOV crop: mask cropped + tokens outside R dropped, p=0.5)
scores.note: About 150 lines on the verified gate_mask path (wrapper.py:81-94, decode_view:259-262, attn_patch:60-64). The planned Z/P9 check (20-step training reproduces the loss columns) cannot pass: training is nondeterministic (measured: two identical seed-0 runs diverge at step 2, 0.97702 vs 0.96150). Cropping the mask brings back a band of the 2a contradiction: inside R, the fuser (2 CXBlocks 7x7, about 6 cells) sees object features beyond R labelled 0. MIN_RETAIN 0.1 allows 90 % cuts, which risks presence drift. The point +0.002 depends on +0.015 invisible recall on the 605, which is 24 % of their 2.53M missed invisible px; E8's round 2, which added real information, moved it only +0.006. The 'outside' oracle the cut targets is only +0.0094 J over 664. Realistic: about 0 to +0.0015, P(G1) about 0.15. No zero-dose control, so a pass cannot be attributed.

scores.arm: B geoset_cut_ft (FOV crop or occluder hole, 1/2 each at p=0.5)
scores.note: Same code as A plus about 20 lines. The hole mode simulates 'no evidence', but at test time an occluded cell has occluder tokens that contradict it. The 'occluded' headroom on good seeds is large (+0.0225 J) but partly Pi3 depth noise on small objects, so the gain is doubtful. It halves A's FOV dose and adds a hole-filling bias, risking spill into depth-separated objects and twins in layered scenes (Breakfast, CoffeeMartini, Barn). B-A is unresolvable at a paired CI of about ±0.003.

scores.arm: C0 adopted baseline geoset_rep_x (not trained)
scores.note: The correct adoption reference. It is not a mechanism control: a same-seed retrain does not reproduce it (measured divergence at step 2 vs the stored fold-0 log), and the 22 under-cover pairs were selected on its own failures (regression-to-mean bias in any arm-C0 contrast on the 22).

scores.arm: M geoset_cut_ft (per-object axis-aligned half-plane token drop, mask and pointer whole, objects >= 20 cells, keep 0.3-0.7, p=0.5)
scores.note: The most faithful simulation: tokens are removed, not relabelled. The memory stays truthful and small objects are never cut. Leakage is at most about 6 cells, and the whole-object pointer is a mild mismatch. About 120 lines. Rng-identity test (d) needs coin, objects and camera logged explicitly, because n_mem/gated_frac depend on predictions. The point +0.0015 assumes 5-15 % recovery of the full reachable ceiling, but the mechanism mainly targets 'outside' (+0.0094 J); net of a 10 % invisible-FP growth (-0.0015 J) the realistic value is about +0.0005. Paired CI for a raw trained arm is about ±0.0025-0.003 (D1 raw vs e11 [-0.0038, +0.0012]), so P(G1) is about 0.15. G2 can fail from one presence flip (D1: CBABasketball -0.0138).

scores.arm: M+ geoset_cutall_ft (same cut, p=1.0)
scores.note: The best single-dose arm for detecting the mechanism. Large objects never train with a whole reference; the predicted-memory recipe drifts (gated_frac and n_mem); G2 risk is higher. It is not a replication of M: it shares M's cut draws and differs in dose. Without a zero-dose retrain, a monotone M < M+ pattern still cannot be separated from retrain draws.

scores.arm: C0 adopted baseline geoset_rep_x
scores.note: As in design 1. It is the base of every composed arm.

scores.arm: N0 geoset_rep_xc_dec = C0 (+) E9-D1 in INV&U (decode-only null composition)
scores.note: Test-set design, the S2-R6 situation. It was measured on the same 664 keyframe pairs with three candidate nulls (D1 +0.0011 pass, D2 +0.0015 pass, r1 +0.0010 fail at -0.0000), and D1 was declared the null afterwards. Its P1/G1 is a post-diction, not a test. As a null it is wrong: D1 trains the decoder too (10.1M vs 5.9M params), so it is not a same-recipe retrain. It is a two-model ensemble that doubles stage-1 decode. A +0.001 keyframe fill with no ownership change transfers like E10 (ratio about 0.5 gives basic about +0.04-0.07; E10's +0.0025 gave +0.088 with CI [-0.034, +0.212]), so E8 adoption is unlikely. Add-only invariants make it safe.

scores.arm: M_c = C0 (+) geoset_mdrop_ft (random-angle half-plane token drop, objects >= 4 cells, kept 0.3-0.9, p=0.5) under the shell
scores.note: Needs the most code: drop training plus compose path, raw, composed and r1 folders, and an in-process compose route. G1 pass is likely but mostly the shell's own +0.001, so the gate stops testing the mechanism. The mechanism margin M_c - N0 is confounded: decoder-trained D1 vs memory-attention-only M, one nondeterministic draw each. The stated '+0.224 on the 22' ceiling ignores the shell's U and 8-connected rules; measured reach is 42.8 % of missed px and a J&F oracle of at most +0.146 on the 22, before the INV restriction. The 4-cell minimum exposes small objects and twins in the raw model, though the shell confines the damage.

scores.arm: W_c = C0 (+) geoset_vwl_ft (region weight lambda=2 on reference-invisible target, both classes) under the shell
scores.note: Its own prediction is about null. In-sample focal mass is already 76 % invisible (design-minimal lossmass_train: 0.726 to 0.883 per-object share at lambda=2), so it rebalances an existing signal. It needs reprojection inside data.load_sample (+35 ms/step) and moving reproj helpers into geomem/. A 2.9 h training to close hypothesis (i) is not worth it in E12.

refuted_claims: Design 0 Z/P9 ('20-step Blocks geoset_pred_ft training reproduces the loss columns of the pre-change run') and design 2 test (a) ('train_one_step loss/grads byte-identical'): training is nondeterministic. Measured: geoset_pred_ft fold 0, seed 0, run twice with unchanged code (40 steps) gives identical step-1 loss 0.13690 but step 2 = 0.97702 vs 0.96150, and the stored adopted log has 0.96201. Any multi-step training loss or grad identity check fails whatever the code change; only rng-stream identity (logged object subsets, coin, memory camera) and single-step forward identity are checkable. (scratchpad/e12-judge-measure/retrain40.out, retrain40b.out)

'E9 D1 = recipe-level retrain / retrain-noise proxy' (design 1 risks, design 0 risks): D1 also trains the mask decoder (config trainable_params 10,112,758 vs 5,922,321; git 645b8b0/b418be0). Its ±0.0023 is the pair-sampling CI of one model pair, not retrain variance. Retrain variance is unmeasured but nonzero.

Design 2 'upper bound of ANY composed arm: +0.041 J over 664 / +0.030 / +0.224 on the 22': this ignores the shell's own U (unclaimed) and 8-connected continuation rules. Measured (host, e12-judge-measure/shell_reach.py): only 42.8 % of the 22 pairs' missed px (61.2 % over 664, 62.9 % on the 605) are in U and connected. Adding ALL missed px there gives J&F +0.146 on the 22, +0.0217 on the 605, +0.0292 on 664, before the INV restriction.

Design 2 'N0 is the required control; the mechanism claim rests on M_c - N0': N0's second model is decoder-trained D1, chosen after three nulls were scored on the test keyframe, so M_c - N0 confounds token dropout with decoder training and with one nondeterministic training draw.

Design 0 'a realistic +0.015 recall_inv on the 605 with unchanged precision (~+0.003 on 664)': +0.015 of their 41.0M invisible GT px is 615k px, 24 % of their 2.53M missed invisible px. E8's round 2, which added real information, moved good-seed invisible recall only +0.006 (0.872 to 0.878). The point estimate is about 2-3x optimistic.

Implicit in designs 0 and 1 (gain driven by the 22 plus the 605 invisible recall): the class a FOV/half-plane cut simulates ('outside') has an oracle of only +0.0094 J over 664 (+0.0052 on the 605) of the +0.041 J invisible oracle (oracle.py on keyframe_vis.json). Most good-seed headroom is 'occluded' (+0.0225 J), partly small-object Pi3 depth noise.
blocking_issues: No design has a zero-dose retrained control. Training is nondeterministic (measured divergence at step 2), and the 22 under-cover pairs are selected on C0's own failures (regression to the mean), so no arm-C0 difference, and especially no under-22 'mechanism signature', can be attributed to token dropout. Add C0' = the new code path with p_cut = 0, same seed and recipe, not adoptable. Contrast arms with it.

The composition shell (design 2: N0, M_c, W_c) was designed and measured on the test keyframe (664 pairs, three nulls, null chosen afterwards), so its G1 pass is a post-diction. Registering it as adoptable in E12 is test-set design like S2-R6. It also hides the mechanism: any second model passes G1 under it. At most it can be a non-adoptable diagnostic lens with a same-recipe null (C0 composed with C0'). Any adoptable shell needs its own registration with the S2-R6 disclosure, G1 declared non-evidential, and stage 2 as the only test.

Training byte/loss identity Z checks (design 0 multi-step loss columns; design 2 grads) are infeasible because training is nondeterministic. As written, the z4/Z4 stage would abort the chain. Replace them with logged rng-stream identity (object subset, extra-memory coin, memory camera, cut draws per step) plus single-step forward-loss identity, and keep the decode byte-identity check (drop=None).
verdicts.recommendation:
Register E12 as a mechanism test, not a headline attempt. Use design 1's cut: per-object axis-aligned half-plane token removal on the 72x72 reference grid, mask and pointer kept whole, objects >= 20 cells, keep 0.3-0.7, applied to the predicted-memory decode and the target decode, nothing at inference. Train three arms through one code path: C0' (p_cut 0, zero-dose retrain control, not adoptable), M (p 0.5) and M+ (p 1.0). If only two trainings fit, use C0' + M+. Budget about 8.7 h of training plus 3 x 8 min decode, one GPU job at a time.

Adoption stays as registered: G1/G2 against C0, then the E8 stage-2 rule. Also require the arm's point Δ against C0' to be > 0, so a lucky retrain draw is not adopted. Report C0' - C0 as the measured retrain draw; it calibrates both G1 and G2's false-fail rate (D1 failed G2 from one lost object).

Pre-register the mechanism verdict on low-noise, pixel-level contrasts arm - C0' with the pair-to-camera-to-scene bootstrap:
- round-1 and final 'outside'-class invisible-GT recall (pixel-weighted and pair-mean, pairs where both masks are present) on the 605 and 664
- invisible-FP px on the 605
- pred/GT px
- dose monotonicity C0' <= M <= M+

Count presence and gate flips separately and keep them out of the mechanism read. Report the under-22 J&F, but do not use it as the signature: one flip moves the 22-pair mean by about ±0.02.

Register realistic predictions: 664 ΔJ&F about 0 to +0.0015 (point about +0.0007), P(G1) about 0.15, P(adoption) under 0.1. The 'outside' ceiling is +0.0094 J. The raw trained-arm CI half-width is about 0.0025-0.003, so the 664-pair gate cannot resolve these arms on J&F alone; the pixel contrasts against C0' can.

Leave out of E12:
- the composition shell as an adoptable arm (test-designed post-diction; D1 is not a same-recipe null; reach on the 22 at most +0.146)
- W_c, since in-sample focal mass is already 76 % invisible
- design 0's mask crop (reintroduces a 2a band) and hole mode (spill-prone, targets noisy 'occluded' pixels)

Replace all training identity checks with rng-stream logging.

scores.arm: A geoset_fov_ft (global FOV rectangle crop of mask + token drop, p 0.5)
scores.note: Gate path verified (GPU probe: per-object per-cell -inf on view 0 changes only that object; pointer-only rows finite). Plumbing correct (SET2_ARMS + PRED_MEM_ARMS), drop passed into encode_reference reaches both reads (train.py:224, :232; with_view keeps views[0], wrapper.py:52-53). Spec bugs: aug_rng constructed twice yet called 'second draw of the same generator'; subset() slices drop[:, i] (wrong axis, should be drop[idx]); Z4's '20-step training reproduces loss columns' is an abort criterion that GPU nondeterminism can trip (grads differ run-to-run). It also CROPS the GT mask (m' = m AND R_full), so the 7x7x2 CXBlock fuser (model_builder.py:349-357) writes 'object features = background' into kept tokens within ~6 cells of the cut and the pointer becomes a part descriptor: a bounded form of the 2a contradiction the design rejects. Objects entirely inside R (r_b = 1) only lose background tokens, so the effective completion dose is lower than the 44 % dropped area suggests. Cost: measured +0.075 s on a 1-memory step with a materialised mask, so about +4 % per fold, within the 1.15x watch.

scores.arm: B geoset_cut_ft (FOV crop or occluder HOLE, 1/2 each at p 0.5)
scores.note: Same code path and same spec bugs as A. The occluded class holds the larger J oracle over 664 (+0.0283 vs outside +0.0094, oracle.py reproduced). But HOLE is a poor simulation: at test time, occluded target cells face existing tokens that show the occluder under another label, not missing tokens. The interior mask crop also puts 'background' labels inside the object's own silhouette band, the strongest 2a-type contradiction of any arm. Hole-filling across depth-separated objects in dense label maps is a real spill risk.

scores.arm: C0 geoset_rep_x (baseline, not trained)
scores.note: Baseline. Numbers verified: J&F 0.9148 re-scored, invisible recall 0.913 / visible 0.971, under22 0.611 (vis_report.txt:188-195).

scores.arm: M geoset_cut_ft (per-object half-plane token drop, whole mask and target, p 0.5)
scores.note: Most correct as written. CUT_ARMS added to BOTH SET2_ARMS and PRED_MEM_ARMS (arms.py:7-8). The drop is attached to ref.views[0] right after encode_reference, so both the memory-camera prediction (train.py:224) and the target decode (:232) see it in all 4 layers. Token index y*72+x matches _pack_view's flatten (wrapper.py:203). The per-object quantile cut guarantees the cut intersects the object, and MIN_KEPT 6 is meaningful (probe: pointer-only gives empty masks). verdicts.recommendation:
Pre-register design 1 (M, with M+ as the dose arm), with design-0 and design-2 elements only where they survive verification.

1. **Core claim is sound.** A per-object, per-cell memory-token drop works through the existing additive attention-mask path, for both the reference view and the predicted view. GPU probe: only the dropped object's logits change, the other 15 stay bitwise identical, and pointer-only rows stay finite. Attached to ref.views[0] right after encode_reference, the drop reaches both reads in a training step (train.py:224 and :232) in all 4 memory-attention layers. The decode path stays byte-identical when off (drop=None). Design 1 is the only one whose plumbing (SET2_ARMS + PRED_MEM_ARMS) and cut rule (relative to each object's own cells, so the cut always hits the object) are correct as written.

2. **Before registering:**
   - (a) Replace every training-side byte-identity check with three things: step-1 loss identity; explicit rng-stream logging (object ids, coin, memory camera, cut parameters) instead of comparing n_mem; and the decode-side Z4 Fencing byte check. Backward is nondeterministic on this GPU, so the training checks as written can abort the chain for nothing.
   - (b) Do not adopt design 0's mask crop. Keep the GT mask whole and drop tokens only. The crop writes background labels into tokens next to the cut through the 7x7x2 fuser, a bounded form of the 2a contradiction design 0 itself rejects. If design 0's rectangle is kept, count as 'cut' only objects that actually lose object cells (r_b < 1).
   - (c) Watch values are fine: the measured mask cost is +0.075 s per 1-memory step, so about +4 % per fold for M and +8 % for M+.

3. **Design 2's composition shell is real** (+0.0011 [+0.0005, +0.0018] for D1, reproduced exactly by an independent re-implementation, and robust to the U correction). It is a decode-only ensemble, outside E12's training goal. If the user wants it, register it as its own decode-only arm. That needs three fixes: U = all C0 PNGs; a rule for contested additions (or drop the overlap invariant); and a decode of D1 with xcl, which has not been measured yet. Its M_c/W_c trained arms are not usable as written: the PRED_MEM_ARMS bug, the 40-80 % vs 20-60 % dose contradiction, and an M_c − N0 contrast confounded by D1's decoder training.

4. **Expected gain is small for every trained arm.** Point estimates are about +0.0015 to +0.0025 on the 664-pair mean, with P(G1) around 0.3. A retrained control would be needed to tell the effect apart from retrain noise (E9 D1 CI half-width about 0.0023).

arms.mechanism:
Simulates a narrower reference camera for each object.

How: all reference-view memory tokens in an axis-aligned half-plane of the 72x72 grid that cuts through the object are removed from the memory cross-attention. Removal is an additive -inf through MemorySet.gate_mask, the path the predicted-memory confidence gate already uses (SDPA mask, attn_patch.py:60-64). The GT memory mask, the 4 pointer tokens and the target GT stay whole.

Effect: target cells whose 3D counterpart lies in the dropped half-plane have no matching key, as an out-of-FOV cell does at test time. The unchanged whole-GT loss then teaches continuation in both directions, because dropped background tokens must still be predicted as background.

Why tokens and not a mask crop: the memory encoder fuses features and label (x = pix_feat_proj + mask; fuser 2 CXBlocks 7x7). A cropped mask would write 'object features = background' into kept tokens near the cut.

Why p = 1.0: it is the maximum dose of the registered distribution. A null here closes the mechanism with no 'dose too low' escape, and together with C0' it gives a clean zero-vs-maximum dose contrast.

Target classes: the outside class (J oracle +0.0094 over 664) faithfully; occlusion only approximately; no-depth pixels not at all.

GPU probe: a per-object, per-cell -inf changes only that object's logits (the other 15 stay bitwise identical), pointer-only rows stay finite, and a materialised zero gate gives logits bitwise equal to the None path.
arms.rule:
Constants (module level, not CLI knobs): CUT_PROB 1.0; CUT_KEEP (0.3, 0.7); CUT_MIN_CELLS 20; CUT_MIN_KEPT 6 (asserted, implied by 0.3 x 20); sides {left, right, top, bottom}.

Per optimiser step (the step counter memory_rng uses), after load_sample and before train_one_step:
1. Create ONE generator per step: g = cut_rng(seed, step) = np.random.default_rng([seed, step, 1]). It is distinct from memory_rng(seed, step) = default_rng([seed, step]). The shared rng (object subsets, the p = 0.5 memory coin) is never touched.
2. u = g.random(); cut iff u < CUT_PROB. The coin is kept so a later p < 1 arm shares the cut parameters.
3. Object cells: C_b = sam3_io.object_cells(ref_masks) = avg_pool2d(mask_inputs(ref_masks, 1008), 14)[:, 0] >= 0.5 on the 72x72 grid. Token index l = y*72 + x, the _pack_view flatten order.
4. For each object b in batch order with n_b = |C_b| >= 20:
   - side = g.integers(4)
   - f = g.uniform(0.3, 0.7), the target kept fraction
   - k = floor((1-f) n_b)
   - coordinate a = x (left), -x (right), y (top), -y (bottom)
   - a_c = sorted(a over C_b)[k]
   - drop[b, l] = True for EVERY grid cell, object or background, with a(l) < a_c.
5. Ties at the cut line are kept, so the realised kept fraction lies in [f, f + max_line_b / n_b]. If no object cell is dropped, the object counts as not cut. Objects under 20 cells draw nothing and are never cut.
6. MemoryView.drop ([B, 5184] bool) is set on ref.views[0] right after encode_reference (train.py:207-208). Both reads in the step therefore see it, in all memory-attention layers: the no-grad memory-camera prediction (train.py:223-225) and the target decode (train.py:232-233).
7. The predicted second memory view carries no drop; its tau 0.7 confidence gate is unchanged. Pointer columns are never dropped. Recipe identical to C0'. Nothing at inference (drop = None).

Logged per step: cut, n_cut, cut_frac (mean realised dropped fraction of object cells), objs, mem_coin, mem_cam.
